extracted.intended_audience: respondents and practitioners involved in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings; OED staff and USPTO counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural limits that govern reciprocal discipline proceedings under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including what grounds trigger reciprocal discipline and whether requests for reconsideration may be entertained. Applies to practitioners facing suspension from practice before the USPTO based on state disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory framework governing reciprocal discipline proceedings before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules governing reciprocal discipline do not permit or authorize parties to file motions for reconsiderations. Without a specific provision for motions for reconsideration in the regulation governing reciprocal discipline, 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, there is no express authority to hear or grant Respondent's Request for Reconsideration. See In re Rheinstein, Proceeding No. D2021-06; In re Bhardwaj, Proceeding No. D2022-24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for reciprocal discipline — 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may be subject to reciprocal discipline when publicly disciplined on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint requested suspension from practice before the USPTO predicated on violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) — i.e., being publicly disciplined on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from appeal/hearing rules (37 C.F.R. § 11.56(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules that apply to appeals or hearings (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.56(c)) are distinct from the reciprocal-discipline framework and their allowances (such as motions) do not carry over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike the USPTO's regulations that govern hearing appeals, including 37 C.F.R. § 11.56(c), the rules governing reciprocal discipline do not permit or authorize parties to file motions for reconsiderations. Thus procedures available in appeal contexts are not implicitly available in reciprocal-discipline proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency must follow its own regulations (Crediford v. Shulkin)
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative agency is bound by its own regulations and cannot grant relief that is not authorized by its rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing Crediford v. Shulkin, 877 F.3d 1040, 1047 (Fed. Cir. 2017): "[A]n agency is bound by its own regulations." This principle supports denial of a motion for reconsideration where the controlling regulation provides no authority to hear such motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome governed by the chosen regulatory framework
rubrics_metrics.description: If a matter is filed pursuant to, and processed according to, the reciprocal-discipline regulatory framework, the framework's provisions control the availability of procedural relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because this matter was filed pursuant to, and was processed according to, the regulatory framework for reciprocal discipline and that framework does not allow for requests for reconsideration, the Respondent's Request for Reconsideration of the Final Order is denied.
